key_insights: This is a JD (law school) admissions vlog, not undergraduate admissions, so it is off-scope for undergrad research
High LSAT/GPA numbers mainly clear a 'can this person do the work' threshold rather than guaranteeing admission
The reader's negative-signal vocabulary (e.g. dull, arrogant, immature-sounding, unclear goals) is what sinks high-numbers candidates more than academics do
For applicants with lower numbers, admission usually hinges on an individualized compelling story (unusual background, strong work experience, clear goals) rather than a repeatable pattern
As numbers move further from the school's median, the rest of the file (essays, resume, grammar) is scrutinized more harshly
A single small mistake is more forgivable when numbers are strong, and less forgivable when numbers are weaker
